lawyer:
S A M Mahbub Elahi with Md. Mizanur Rahman Bhuiyan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners. 
No one appears ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Gulshan Ara Begum alias Jahanara and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Moazzen Hossain Chowdhury and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Md. Mozammel Hoque J: In this Rule issued under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 are directed to show cause as to why the order No. 78 dated 9.3.89 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 1987 rejecting an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 95 of 1982 should not be set aside. 

 3. It. is their case that on 21.4.87 they first came to know from plaintiff No. 2 Moazzem Hossain Chowdhury that the plaintiffs obtained a decree for partition in the court. Thereafter the petitioner No. 3 came to Court on 22.4.87 and enquired about this ex parte decree. Then he filed an application for certified copies of the impugned decree and other necessary papers on 22.4.87. He got the certified copy of the decree on 26.4.87 and then an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed before the Court on 25.5.87 which is, according to them, very much within the statutory period of 30 days to file an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in paragraphs 4 and 8 the petitioners categorically stated that the summons were not served upon them and for that reason they were not aware of the aforesaid suit or the date of hearing of the suit. They further asserted that they filed an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure within the statutory period from the date of their knowledge. This application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 61 of 1987. 

 4. From the records it appears that the notices were served upon the opposite parties about the aforesaid miscellaneous case. Opposite parties appeared before the Court on 15.2.89 and filed an application praying for time for filing written objection and the time was given upto 22.2.89 for filing written objection. But ultimately the, opposite parties did not appear and file any written objection. So the Miscellaneous Case was heard ex parte and dismissed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka on 9.3.81 after hearing the present petitioner. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order dated 9.3.89 the petitioners preferred this revisional application and obtained the present Rule. 

 6. Mr. S A M Mahbub Elahi, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that in the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure the petitioners have asserted that the application was filed within statutory period and that he did not receive any notice whatsoever about the Title Suit No. 95 of 1982 after the death of their predecessor-in-interest defendant No. 1. Mr. Elahi submits that ex parte decree was passed on 29.1.87 but the petitioners were not aware of the hearing date of the suit. On 21.4.87 they came to know about the aforesaid decree from one of the opposite parties. Thereafter on 22.4.87 they went to the Court, enquired into the matter and found that the ex parte decree was passed on 21.9.87. On the same day they filed an application for certified copy of the aforesaid decree which they got on 26.4.87. Mr. Elahi submits that if these 5 days arc deducted, then the application is found very much within time, that is, within 30 days from the date of their knowledge. The learned Subordinate Judge by the impugned order dismissed the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure holding that the ex pane decree was passed on 21.4.87 and the instant Miscellaneous Case was filed on 25.5.87 and as such it was time barred. The learned Subordinate Judge has not at all considered the fact that it took 5 days in between to obtain the certified copies of the ex pane decree and other papers. If the time is calculated from 21.4.87 to 25.5.87, after excluding the time taken for obtaining the certified copies, it clearly appears that the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed within the statutory period. So, we find that the learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law in computing the period of limitation in the present case. The learned Subordinate Judge further held that there was no separate application for condonation of delay in filing the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This finding is of no substance in view of the fact that we have already held that the application was filed within statutory period of limitation. 

 8. Record shows that summons were allegedly served upon the petitioners by hanging on 28.9.86 and the process server submitted report on 29.9.86, 30.9.86 was fixed in the summons for appearance of the substituted defendants. On 30.9.86 an order was passed fixing 29.1.87 for ex pane hearing. Process server has written names of two persons showing them as witnesses for service of summons. But the alleged two witnesses did not put their signatures on the summons. No summons were issued under registered post. From the above it appears that the fixing of ex pane hearing date on 29.1.87 by an order dated 30.9.86 is contrary to the provisions of Order 9 rule 6(c) of the Code of Civil Procedure which finds support from the case of M/s. Adamjee Jute Mills Ltd. Vs. Chairman, 3rd Labour Court, 1988 BLD page 1. Further, the provisions of Order 5 rule 9B of the Code of Civil Procedure have not been complied with as no summons were issued upon the petitioners by registered post with A/D. 

 9. On 29.1.87 PW Moazzem Hossain Chowdhury was examined and thereafter the ex parte decree was passed on the same date, that is, on 29.1.87. Now from the orders dated 30.9.86 and 29.1.87 it appears that just after the alleged service of notice by hanging next date was fixed for ex pane hearing of the suit without affording any opportunity to the present petitioners to file any written statement. It is the specific case of the present petitioners that though they were substituted they were not at all aware of the date of hearing of Title Suit No. 95 of 1982. So, the learned Subordinate Judge in fact committed an error of law in not deciding this aspect as to whether the notices were duly served upon the present petitioners before fixing date for ex pane hearing. But from the order sheet it clearly appears to us that though the notices were shown to have been served upon the present petitioners by hanging in fact they had not been given any reasonable opportunity to defend their case in view of the fact that just after the alleged service of notice, the ex pane hearing date was fixed and on that date ex parte decree was passed. 

 10. The learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law in not fixing any date for taking steps by the substituted heirs of the defendant No. 1 who admittedly died before filing any written statement. In a case like this we are of the view that the learned Subordinate Judge, before fixing the suit for ex parte hearing, must satisfy itself that the notices were duly served upon the substituted heirs but no such satisfaction has been recorded in the order dated 30.9.86. Moreover, records did not show that notices were issued both through the usual course of process server and under registered post. Our above view finds support from the case of Syed Anisul Huq Vs. MN Arif, 40 DLR 314. It is a partition suit and the decree passed in such a hot haste just after alleged service of notice cannot be sustained in law. 

 11. In that view of the matter we hold that the summons were not duly served upon the petitioners in accordance with law and the learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law in his decision resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No. 61 of 1987 and rejecting the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the above circumstances we feel that ends of justice will be met, if we set aside the ex parte decree dated 29.1.87 and restore the original suit to its file and number. 

 12. In the result, this Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned order dated 9.3.89 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 61 of 1987 is set aside, the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is allowed, ex parte decree dated 29.1.87 is set aside and the Title Suit No. 95 of 1988 is restored to its file and number.
